title: Ordinary quotient sequence adjunction and constant-ring factorization
statement: For every prime l, finite extension E of Q_l and scheme W, the actual quotient coefficient sequence projection has ordinary adjoints O as in [def-pur-sequence-adjoint-resolution-data], and a ringed factorization through the constant completed ring. The first morphism has identity geometric inverse image, structural map given by the completed-ring quotient projections, and exact scalar-restriction module direct image. Constant-ring sequence modules identify with towers of base modules, preserving sections and horizontal maps, and the second module direct image identifies with inverse limit. All composition, ordinary tensor, quotient-transition and transpose equations are the fields of PurSequenceOrdinaryAdjoints and PurSequenceRingedFactorization. No finite-type or field-of-definition hypothesis is needed. See [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site] for the actual categories.

source.place: Coefficient-comparison paragraph, via original sequence-projection normalization proof steps.

proof.text: Form the completed-ring cone on the actual quotient tower, using naturality of its limit projections. Use the explicit ordinary portion of the sequence-site constant/limit construction and its tensor/limit module adjunction. No derived construction or proof that this cone is limiting is needed for this ordinary step.

Compare the level scalar extensions with the recorded finite adjunctions by uniqueness of left adjoints. Identify the actual quotient mate first as a natural transformation by uniqueness of its specified components. The unit comparisons and this quotient mate formula identify the horizontal tensor transitions on all local unit tensors; scalar-extension Hom extensionality gives the transition equation. Identify the evaluation comparison with equality transport, so composition of equality maps gives the prescribed limit-coordinate projection formula. The generic adjunction unit equation and naturality of those projections give the ordinary transpose formula.

Construct PurSequenceOrdinaryAdjoints explicitly from the ordinary constant/limit geometry, the additive strict scalar-extension functor, its adjunction, the finite left-adjoint uniqueness comparisons, the normalized horizontal transition equations and the limit-coordinate transpose. Apply the constant-ring factorization theorem to this constructed O and return the pair.
